subject: refactor: stop coercing invalid attribute values in gen2 components (#6926)
changeset:
---
'@adobe/spectrum-wc-core': patch
'@adobe/spectrum-wc': patch
---

`Accordion` — Stopped writing a clamped `level` back to the DOM. The value you set stays on the attribute and property, and a development warning names it. Item headings render the nearest valid level for any other number, rounded and then clamped (`1` renders `h2` and `7` renders `h6`, as before; `4.6` renders `h5`), and the default `h3` for anything else, which previously rendered a broken heading such as `<hNaN>`. A numeric string such as `"4"`, as set by frameworks, renders `h4` without a warning. Removing `level` or `density` resets it to its default without a warning. `swc-accordion-item` now warns on an invalid `size` and renders its chevron at the default size.

'@adobe/spectrum-wc-core': patch
'@adobe/spectrum-wc': patch
---

`Action Group` — Fixed arrow-key navigation for an invalid `orientation`: it now uses the default horizontal direction. An invalid `static-color` is no longer passed to child buttons, so they render their default. Both now warn through the standard development warning.

---
'@adobe/spectrum-wc-core': patch
'@adobe/spectrum-wc': patch

`Avatar` — Stopped rewriting an invalid `size` to `100`. The value you set stays on the attribute and property, a development warning names it, and the avatar renders at the default size. Invalid markup such as `size="banana"` is no longer rewritten to `size="NaN"`. A numeric string such as `"200"`, as set by frameworks, no longer warns; the property returns it as set.

`Meter` — Stopped rewriting an invalid `variant` to `informative`. The value you set stays on the attribute and property, a development warning names it, and the fill renders in the default informative color.

`Meter`, `Progress Bar` — Added a development warning when `min-value` is greater than `max-value`, when either bound is not a number, or when `value` is not a number. The values stay as set, and the bar renders the corrected range and value. Non-numeric markup such as `value="banana"` is no longer rewritten to `value="NaN"`. Fixed numeric strings such as `"50"`, as set by frameworks, rendering as 0. Removing `value`, `min-value`, `max-value`, `label-position`, or `static-color` now resets it to its default without a warning.

`Progress Circle` — Stopped writing a clamped `progress` back to the attribute and property. The value you set is kept, a development warning names an out-of-range value, and the circle and `aria-valuenow` render it clamped to 0–100. Non-numeric markup such as `progress="banana"` is kept instead of being rewritten to `progress="NaN"`, warns, and renders 0%. Fixed a numeric string such as `"50"`, as set by frameworks, rendering as 0%. Removing `static-color` no longer warns.
